item.research_question: How can mechanical properties of refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) and refractory complex concentrated alloys (RCCAs) be systematically compiled and visualized to guide their development as structural materials?
item.material_system: 122 refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) and refractory complex concentrated alloys (RCCAs) containing five or more elements with concentrations between 5 and 35 at% (RHEAs) or three or more principal elements with concentrations beyond 35% (RCCAs)
item.processing_route: Compilation of data from published reports (2010 to January 2018); metallurgical states include non-equilibrium (as-cast), optimized (homogenization/annealing), hot isostatic pressing (HIP), cold rolling (CR), spark plasma sintering (SPS), and severe plastic deformation (SPD)
item.test_conditions: Uniaxial loading (tension or compression) with strain rates ≤ 10⁻³ s⁻¹; temperature range from −268.8 °C (4.2 K) to 1600 °C (1873 K)
key_findings: The dataset contains 340 mechanical tests on 122 compositions.
All reported RHEAs and RCCAs crystallize with at least one phase with body centered cubic (BCC) structure.
Yield strength and specific yield strength were visualized as a function of temperature for single-phase and multiphase alloys.
Yield stress was plotted against alloy density at room temperature and 800 °C.
Alloy densities were calculated using the Rule of Mixtures (ROM).
Young's moduli for single-phase alloys were estimated using ROM.
item.mechanism: The authors do not propose a physical mechanism for deformation; instead, they argue that the compiled data allows for the visualization of property evolution with temperature and density to identify material solutions for specific applications.
item.limitations: The data is limited to studies published through the end of January 2018 and only includes mechanical tests with strain rates less than or equal to 10⁻³ s⁻¹.
item.future_work: The data compilation can enable machine learning and data analytics methods to extract insights and trends not available from individual studies, thus accelerating the development of these alloys.
quotes: The comprehensive data compilation provides up-to-date mechanical properties of RHEAs and RCCAs tested under uniaxial loading on the basis of published reports from 2010 through the end of January 2018.
It can be seen from Table 1 of the data sheet that RHEAs and RCCAs have been studied over a wide temperature range between −268.8 °C (4.2 K) and 1600 °C (1873 K).
